title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Order Disapproving a Proposed Rule Change To List and Trade Shares of the NYDIG Bitcoin ETF Under NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Commodity-Based Trust Shares)
summary: On 16 March 2022, the Federal Register published an SEC order (Release No. 34-94395, File No. SR-NYSEArca-2021-57) disapproving NYSE Arca's proposed rule change to list and trade shares of the NYDIG Bitcoin ETF under NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E, the exchange's Commodity-Based Trust Shares listing standard. NYSE Arca filed the proposal on 30 June 2021; the Commission instituted proceedings on 29 September 2021 and issued this order on 10 March 2022. The trust's sponsor is NYDIG Asset Management LLC, with NYDIG Trust Company LLC, chartered by the New York State Department of Financial Services, as bitcoin custodian. The Commission concluded NYSE Arca had not met its burden under Exchange Act Section 6(b)(5). Among its findings, the record did not establish a reasonable likelihood that manipulating the ETP would require trading on the CME bitcoin futures market — the test the order uses to decide whether CME constitutes a market of significant size under NYSE Arca's surveillance-sharing arrangement.
why_it_matters: This March 2022 order applies the same Exchange Act Section 6(b)(5) fraud-and-manipulation standard used in the SEC's other bitcoin exchange-traded product decisions, this time finding the record did not show that manipulating the proposed ETP would require trading on the CME bitcoin futures market. Naming NYDIG Asset Management LLC and NYDIG Trust Company LLC here reflects only what the SEC's own order states about their proposed roles.
